categories.finding: Captions and diagrams make the reporting problem and assistant role readable silently. Actual case completion remains unseen.
The opening puts viewers behind the pathologist at screens; later overlays sit beside the speaker to isolate the proposed flow.
About 25s establish the reporting problem before the team appears; the main flow explanation occupies about 11s, followed by positioning.
The blank cursor and required fields are answered by an organized specimen report, but no final clinician review is shown.
Patient context and administrative friction may create empathy with the specialist; team shots may suggest approachability. Response is unmeasured.
The repeated line-wave-to-text motif links explanation and closing identity; the same case is not tracked across all source screens.
Accuracy, LIS compatibility, personalization and workforce percentage are presented claims. Clinical performance and the statistical source were not independently checked.
Pathology-specific terms and the voice-to-report motif give Voquill a clear domain identity.
Show one observation entering the correct report field and the pathologist reviewing it before sign-out.
